p: What are resources that you provide to commercial corridors that are in the process of forming a BID?

My team provides extensive resources, technical assistance to any neighborhood that is interested in forming a BID. We attend all of the steering committees once they are formed. Even before a steering committee is formed, any interested stakeholder, we provide them with what we call the BID One-on-One about the essentials that are needed, what a steering committee should comprise of, so we provide a lot of resources for the formation and throughout the process.

COMMITTEE ON SMALL BUSINESS 17 a BID? What are obstacles and what are resources that you provide so they could overcome those obstacles?

Some of the obstacles is getting that broad-based support. Everyone is not a fan of BID, but part of that is providing the education so my team provides a lot of resources to those steering committees to make sure that they're communicating properly what a BID is, what a BID does, what is entailed in the BID process so that it's clear to those stakeholders what that process looks like, timeline, budget, resources, and all those things that are required.

Okay. We have approximately 75, 76 BIDs in the state of New York, 26 in Manhattan, but we don't even have half of that in Brooklyn and in the Bronx so what are factors that you would say are playing a role in terms of boroughs of Manhattan and the Bronx not having BIDs compared to the numbers of all the boroughs?

There are 12 BIDs in the Bronx, there are 22 in Brooklyn, 26 in Manhattan, 11 in Queens, and 4 in Staten Island. When it comes to BIDs, it's really about the location that has to consist of commercial corridors so there's a

There are certain properties that are not assessed, whether they're City-owned, so we help them work through some of those issues to come up with reasonable boundaries for what a BID looks like.

We have 10 BIDs that are in our BID formation pipeline so we're hoping to see a lot more BIDs in the future, especially with the additional resources that the Mayor's Administration has provided us so we can provide that additional assistance through the BID formation process.
